Aim and objectives

Aim. To explain the integrated neurobiology of mood disorders, psychosis, suicidality, functional symptoms and delirium for MRCPsych Paper A.

At the end of this chapter, you should be able to:

  1. Describe HPA axis, neurotrophic (BDNF), inflammatory and circuit models of depression.
  2. Outline the biology of bipolar disorder, including heritability, circadian rhythm, dopamine and mitochondrial dysfunction.
  3. Explain increased presynaptic striatal dopamine synthesis and NMDA receptor hypofunction in schizophrenia.
  4. Describe cognitive deficits in schizophrenia, such as slowed processing and poor working memory, that predate psychosis.
  5. Explain the stress-diathesis model of suicide.
  6. Describe predictive processing models of functional symptoms, and cholinergic and inflammatory models of delirium.
  7. Answer the chapter's 109 exam-style questions, scoring at least 80%, by the end of this chapter.
